findings.trigger: Edit an existing task in the panel, set cycle 'cron' and cron_string '*/5 * * *' (four fields) or any cron/weekly/monthly schedule for which calculate_next_run() yields no next run -> _update_task_with_data never calls unreadable_cron_reason() (only add_task does, lines 602-606), and its deactivation check at 1025 covers only CYCLE_ONCE ('task.cycle == CYCLE_ONCE and task.next_run_ts and ...'), whereas add_task at 624 also switches off on 'next_run_ts is None'. The task is saved ACTIVE with next_run_ts None and the panel answers 'Task ... updated successfully'. It never runs; the next page load calls it expired and switches it off. The unreadable_cron_reason docstring describes exactly this defect as fixed 'before a task is stored' - it is fixed on the add path and still open on the edit path (two places doing the same thing have drifted).
findings.suggestion: In _update_task_with_data, after _update_task_schedule_details, refuse with unreadable_cron_reason(task) when it is not None, and mirror add_task's rule: 'task.next_run_ts is None or (CYCLE_ONCE and in the past)' switches the task off and the message says so (or refuse the edit outright when no next run can be computed).
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see tasks_bp.py (the route may validate the cron string before calling the service, as it does for 'options'), nor whether ScheduledTask.is_valid() or calculate_next_run() rejects a four-field cron itself. The docstring at 145-152 says neither did.

findings.trigger: A one-time task is due at 12:00:00. The operator has the task page open (or refreshes it) at 12:00:03, before the scheduler's tick has executed the task -> _calculate_frontend_status sees 'cycle == once and next_run_ts < current_time', sets is_active = False and _save_updated_tasks writes that through scheduler.update_task. The scheduler then finds the task inactive and never starts/stops/restarts the container. The page shows 'expired'; nothing tells the operator that the action was skipped rather than done. The same window exists for a task the scheduler is late for (heavy load, restart of DDC).
findings.suggestion: Do not treat 'next_run_ts < now' alone as expired for an active one-time task; only deactivate when the scheduler has marked it (status 'completed', or a missed/failed marker) or when it is past by more than the scheduler's tick plus grace. Better: the listing should never write state that decides whether a task runs - leave that to the scheduler and only display.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see scheduler.py: whether the scheduler runs due tasks from its own memory regardless of the file, how long its tick is, and whether update_task() from a web thread changes the copy the scheduler loop reads. The recent commit title 'Listing the tasks no longer switches off a one-time task still to run' (f163ceac, after the reviewed commit) suggests this was real.

findings.trigger: A timezone string pytz does not know reaches the service - the config 'timezone' with a typo, or (for list_tasks/add_task, which take request.timezone_str first) a browser-supplied IANA name newer than the installed pytz, e.g. 'Europe/Kyiv' or 'America/Ciudad_Juarez' -> pytz.timezone() raises UnknownTimeZoneError, which is a subclass of KeyError. Every fallback in this file catches (ImportError, AttributeError) and (ValueError, ...) but not KeyError: _get_timezone_abbreviation (1155-1161), _format_timestamp_local (802-808), _debug_time_conversion (551-556), _debug_calculated_time (658-663). The exception escapes to the public method and the WHOLE call fails: get_task_form_data -> 'Data error loading form data: 'Europe/Kyiv'', list_tasks -> 'Data error listing tasks: ...' (no task is shown at all), add_task -> 'Data error adding task: ...' from a DEBUG helper that should never decide the outcome. The 'Fallback to timezone identifier' branches never run for the one failure they were written for.
findings.suggestion: Catch pytz.UnknownTimeZoneError (or KeyError) in the four helpers and fall back as intended; validate request.timezone_str in _determine_timezone and fall back to the config timezone when pytz does not know it; make the _debug_* helpers unable to fail the request.
findings.unsure_why: Sure that UnknownTimeZoneError subclasses KeyError and that no helper catches it. Unsure whether the timezone can actually be invalid here: the config form and the tasks route (not visible) may validate it before it reaches the service.

findings.trigger: POST /api/watchdog/maintenance with a configured container but without 'minutes' -> line 319 calls pause(container, int(0), ...) inside the try; if pause() accepts 0 (or None-like input) the pause is set. Line 321 then evaluates int(data.get('minutes')) = int(None) OUTSIDE the try -> TypeError -> Flask 500. The pause exists but the caller is told the request failed; the action log line is never written (log_user_action runs after the failing int()). The two reads of 'minutes' also disagree (default 0 at 319, none at 321).
findings.suggestion: Parse minutes once, before pause(), into a local (minutes = int(data.get('minutes', 0))) inside the try, refuse minutes <= 0 explicitly, and reuse the local at 321-322.
findings.unsure_why: services/automation/maintenance.pause is not visible; if it raises ValueError for 0 minutes, the request answers 400 'bad_minutes' before line 321 and only the duplicated parsing remains. The panel probably always sends minutes, so the trigger needs a hand-made request or a future form change.

findings.trigger: get_task_management_service() returns one shared instance, and add_task keeps per-request state in self.cron_error (reset at 198, set at 603, read at 203). Two add_task calls in parallel waitress threads: A stores a cron error message, B's 'self.cron_error = None' at 198 runs in between -> A reports the generic 'Task validation failed or next run time could not be calculated' instead of the cron reason; or B's is_valid() fails and B reports A's cron message about a cron string B never sent.
findings.suggestion: Return the reason instead of storing it on the instance (have _validate_and_calculate_next_run return (ok, reason)) or use a local variable.

findings.trigger: check_auth_rate_limit brakes only requests that carry an Authorization header (232-235) and /setup (226). The form login introduced with the session binding (login.login_page, referenced at 350) posts username and password in the request body with no Authorization header, so a script POSTing 1,000 passwords per minute to the login form passes this limiter untouched, while the same guesses via Basic auth are cut off at 100/min. The module comment at 81-98 still describes Basic as the only way credentials arrive.
findings.suggestion: Either put the login-form POST path under the same (or the 5/min) limiter here, or confirm and document that app/blueprints/login (not visible) applies its own limiter, so the two do not drift.
findings.unsure_why: The login blueprint is outside this section; it may already call setup_limiter/auth_limiter or its own. The 600,000-iteration hash (~85 ms per check) also slows brute force independently of any limiter.

findings.trigger: Add a recurring task for which calculate_next_run() returns None (a cron expression that is syntactically valid but never occurs, e.g. '0 0 31 2 *', or a weekly/monthly schedule the scheduler cannot resolve) -> line 624 switches it off because 'next_run_ts is None', and the answer at 224-226 says 'Task added, but switched off: the time given is in the past, so it will not run. Set a new time to switch it on.' No time is in the past; a new time will not help. This is the same wrong-reason message the unreadable_cron_reason docstring (148-152) describes, still produced for the None case.
findings.suggestion: Keep the reason from _validate_and_calculate_next_run (past time vs. no next run computable) and word the message accordingly.

notes: Observed but without a trigger I can state from this section alone: (1) edit_task/_update_task_with_data mutates the task object from find_task_by_id (container, action, cycle, all schedule fields cleared at 1087-1092) BEFORE is_valid() at 1013; if find_task_by_id hands out the scheduler's live in-memory object rather than a fresh load, a refused edit leaves that object half-edited until the next reload. Same pattern in update_task_status: _prepare_task_activation recomputes next_run and clears last_run_error before the refusal at 326. (2) update_task_status catches (ValueError, TypeError) but not KeyError (all sibling methods do); a pytz KeyError from calculate_next_run would surface as an unhandled 500. (3) list_tasks reverts is_active by matching task_data.get('id') against task.task_id; this relies on to_dict() renaming task_id to id as the comment at 276-278 says - not verifiable here. (4) toggle_rule round-trips rule.to_dict() into update_rule(); whether update_rule accepts every key to_dict emits (id, metadata, validation_warnings) and whether it re-validates and could refuse a stored rule is outside this section. (5) test_rule builds channel_id/guild_id '0' when the caller omits them; if _pre_filter_rules filters by channel, a dry run without channel_id silently shows no matches. Whether _check_match has side effects (cooldowns, state) in a dry run is not visible. (6) start_maintenance records by=f'panel:{session_user() or "admin"}' - a Basic-auth caller with a non-admin web_ui_user is logged as 'admin'; auth.current_user() would be exact. (7) verify_password's setup path writes session['setup_mode'] = True; nothing in this section clears it after the password is set. (8) create_app in app/__init__.py is a bare Flask factory with no blueprints or auth wired; if anything uses it, it serves an app without login_required routes - most likely dead or test-only, cannot tell. (9) auth_error catches only RuntimeError and discord errors around load_config(); any other exception from load_config turns a 401 into a 500. (10) The revert in list_tasks restores is_active but leaves frontend_status 'expired' for an unsaved task, which is the truthful display. (11) 'is_in_past' at 735 is None (JSON null) rather than False when next_run_ts is None - cosmetic. (12) SPEC B11/B12 are respected: web tasks carry WEB_UI_CREATOR and no channel; nothing here adds a channel check.
